description: Bug report from a user of the packaging library: Requirement("demo-lib===") is accepted and prints back as demo-lib===, although the arbitrary equality operator === has nothing to compare against there (=== is meant for arbitrary, non-PEP 440 version strings). Find the problem and fix it. Change files under src/packaging/ only.
environment: Python >= 3.13 stdlib; base tree = pypa/packaging 2c87a33 (src, tests, licenses, pyproject, README), no repository history; the project's own test suite needs pytest, which is not installed
visible_checks: python -c "from src.packaging.requirements import Requirement; print(Requirement('demo-lib>=1'))" (from the workspace root; pytest is not available)
provenance: real fix: pypa/packaging commit 2aada00 (fix: reject empty arbitrary versions in requirements, #1430, 2026-10-06), base = its parent 2c87a33; reference/good.patch is that commit's src diff; symptom-only description naming Requirement only; hidden cases authored for agent-benchmark (2026-10-11): the reported entry point, the inferred SpecifierSet entry point and two non-empty === guards; other reference patches built by build_task.py. Public repository: contamination possible; v2 (2026-10-11, before any graded run): the description no longer says 'a version string', which invited the over-strict reading that === needs a real version
